title: Many third-party credits concentrated into a small number of accounts
definition: A set of accounts receiving credits from a large number of distinct third-party originators, with the credits then consolidated into one or a few downstream accounts. The indicator measures the concentration of originators and the consolidation that follows; it does not identify who the originators are or what their relationship is.
evidence_to_cite: the list of originators with the count of credits per originator
the downstream accounts and the consolidation totals
the account opening dates and the customer due diligence file for each account
benign_explanations: A payment gateway account that legitimately receives credits from many merchants and pays out to a settlement account.
A charitable or membership organisation collecting individual donations and remitting them to a central fund.
A ride-share or delivery platform that credits drivers on the customer's behalf.
An employer payroll process that credits employees' accounts and consolidates statutory deductions.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, guidance on money laundering and funnel accounts, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
